decision: ACCEPT Peerit release sequence 28 as the LIVE bounded-public-test launch successor carrying the T2 CELL.PUT browser-write half: the signed limited Cell-PUT authority profile (peerit-limited-cell-put-profile-v1.json) and the pure-JS/WebCrypto pow-issuance-v1 spend provider ride the signed web closure, so a stock browser can author a record, obtain a PoW admission token from the live issuer, CELL.PUT the sealed record to BOTH live relays with verified receipts and byte-exact readback, then render locally. Writes are explicit user actions only (networkPuts 1, mode explicit-user-writes); ordinary feed delivery remains LOCAL_ONLY and the read path is byte-exact unchanged (limited Cell-GET profile re-issued at 28 with identical semantics). INBOX work is explicitly excluded (discovery half is a separate assignment against the rebuilt browser artifact). The exact production CSP remains unchanged, authenticated browser authority MUST become active before any relay I/O, recovery performs zero network PUTs, the all-five successor remains excluded, and the GA product gate remains blocked with all 22 blockers disclosed-open.

authority.owner_instruction: Ship the CELL.PUT half of the T2 browser-write milestone: a stock browser authors a record (comment/post), obtains a PoW admission token from the live issuer, CELL.PUTs the sealed record to BOTH live relays with verified receipts + byte-exact readback, then renders locally. Explicitly NO INBOX work (the vendored blind client has no INBOX constructors; that half waits for the relay-lane upstream artifact rebuild). Worktree ends clean on the branch tip.

root_cause.mechanism: Browser writes were parked: the signed limited Cell-GET authority pins networkPuts 0 and ordinaryDelivery local-only, so the outbox flush queue never ran. The relay lane (T2-A) shipped pow-issuance-v1 — an OPEN fleet write admission profile (schemeId 1, profileId 8, conformanceClass 1, roleBits 49, parameterUrl null) with a public issuer per relay — so permissionless writes are now possible without host keys. This half ships the browser side: a CSP-safe spend provider (challenge -> pure-JS/WebCrypto PoW at 20 bits -> /redeem -> one-use token presentation) wired into the existing createAdmissionProvider seam, plus the signed limited Cell-PUT authority profile that pins the exact write posture. One record per authored item; the two relay slots are ordered by relay-public-key byte order (syd-1 52f4... slot 0, dal-1 8b3f... slot 1); ONE /redeem per record mints a 2-slot token over the binding root of both ordered request commitments, and each relay receives token || itsSlot || otherSlots as its CELL.PUT admission presentation.
correction_applied: js/substrate/pow-issuance-spend-provider.mjs: pure-JS/WebCrypto/CSP-safe pow-issuance-v1 spend provider + createPowIssuanceV1AdmissionProviderFactory; byte primitives asserted byte-identical to the relay lane's token-codec.js (binding root, preimage, leading-zero-bits, presentation).

js/substrate/limited-cell-put-profile.mjs + peerit-limited-cell-put-profile-v1.json: verifyPeeritLimitedCellPutProfileV1 validator + the deterministic ceremony-signed profile source pinning the exact write authority (see pow_issuance_binding).

Flush wiring without flush-machinery changes: the admissionProviderFor seam drives the factory, the provider feeds createRelayAdapter, and createCellReplica spreads createAdmissionProvider at install time.

test/peerit-pow-issuance-spend.mjs: local dual-relay drill — ONE mint covered both relays (20 bits, allowance 2, redeem calls 1), CELL.PUT STORED + signature-valid on both, byte-exact CELL.GET readback on both, replay idempotent, re-slot/bad-PoW/expired/foreign-key all rejected, added to the package.json test chain.

pow_issuance_binding.parameterHash_semantics: descriptor-driven (rotates with the fleet; taken from the current signature-verified descriptor at runtime — the release profile deliberately pins NO admission parameter hash)
pow_issuance_binding.one_token_per_record: ONE /redeem per authored record mints exactly one 2-slot token bound to the binding root of the two slot-ordered request commitments; a second mint for the same record is never attempted
pow_issuance_binding.slot_order: relay-public-key byte order: syd-1 (52f4d783...) slot 0, dal-1 (8b3f4161...) slot 1
pow_issuance_binding.issuer_relay_key: identical on both relays (2f64e5f3..., shared issuer master key); issuer origins pinned per relayPublicKey in the authority profile because the vendored VerifiedAdmissionParameters brand exposes only parameterHash client-side
pow_issuance_binding.cost_units: relay-internal WAL/quota metadata (CELL.PUT sizeClass 1/2 x leaseClass 1/2 = 10..280 costUnits); never computed or enforced client-side
pow_issuance_binding.mint_performance: the in-browser mint must land a 20-bit proof far inside the issuer's 120s challenge TTL: the vendored noble-hashes SHA-256 inner loop (pure JS, strict-CSP safe) measures ~160k candidates/s in headless Chromium (p50 7.1s, p99 17.6s over 12 mints at 20 bits — scripts/browser-peerit-pow-issuance-bench.mjs); a challenge that outlives the mint is a liveness event, never a verification failure — the mint restarts from a FRESH challenge (bounded 3 attempts, abortable), and invalid-proof rejections (POW_INSUFFICIENT_WORK) are never retried
pow_issuance_binding.record_commitment: HMAC-SHA256(key=BIND, count‖c₀‖…‖c_{allowance-1}) — the DEPLOYED fleet design (00-core/hiverelay packages/blind-daemon/pow-issuance-v1/token-codec.js); the superseded blake2b256 design (retired v1-integration checkout) is never used. Relay-lane handoff 2026-08-07: the fleet verifier rejects blake2b-bound tokens (observed as canonical INTERNAL/code-17 on dal-1 across two drill runs, nothing stored); the two fleet binding-root vectors are pinned verbatim in test/peerit-pow-issuance-spend.mjs (b)
pow_issuance_binding.in_record_pow: UNCHANGED — the app-level comment-14/post-16-bit PoW is still minted at author time and verified by every client on ingest; the pow-issuance token is IN ADDITION to it, not a replacement
pow_issuance_binding.relay_blindness: relays stay blind: sealed records, hash-addressed cells, zero relay trust; the issuer sees a challenge-bound record commitment, not content
pow_issuance_binding.operator_trust_boundary: issuer and relay are operator-run; unlinkability is operator-trust at v1, the same boundary as the relays today (lane plan D2 honesty note)
